text: [issue by dti131] ### Bug Description Create Train Tracks cause large framerate drops, especially curved tracks. Using Spark profiler I was able to find that it's specifically this: ### Reproduction Steps - Install Create and Sodium on Neoforge 1.21.1 - Place train tracks, ideally curved (in an empty superflat world to ensure that there is nothing else causing the drop) - Run a Spark profiler while looking at the train tracks and another while not looking at them or observe your framerate. - Note: for some reason F3+C didn't allow me to force a crash (probably keyboard issues) but I'll upload an unrelated crash report anyway. ### Log File [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31036282/latest.log) ### Crash Report [crash-2026-08-11_18.50.13-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31036302/crash-2026-08-11_18.50.13-client.txt) [comment by douira (contributor)] Give us the spark profile and not just a screenshot [comment by jellysquid3 (member)] `glMultiDrawElementsBaseVertex` taking time is not evidence of a problem in Sodium. OpenGL drivers will execute commands asynchronously, and if the command buffer gets too full, this will cause random OpenGL rendering functions to appear slow.
